speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in view of the winding down of the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) in September 2021 (a) whether there will be an increase in retrenchment and unemployment, especially in the aviation, aerospace and hospitality sectors; and (b) how will the Ministry support the companies and workers in these sectors which have limited scope for recovery in the near term.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), the Government has been providing targeted support to these sectors that are affected very badly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Workforce Singapore (WSG) has rolled out various Job Redesign Reskilling Programmes to support employers in these sectors to make use of the downtime to re-design jobs and re-skill their employees to take on new job roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For affected workers who are looking to switch to new careers in other sectors, we will help them access suitable jobs and skills opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides WSG’s Careers Connect and NTUC’s e2i career centres, WSG has set up the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres in all Housing and Development Board towns and deployed Careers Connect On-the-Go to bring career matching services closer to jobseekers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Jobseekers can also tap on digital resources available on WSG’s MyCareersFuture portal to search for suitable job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will continue to closely monitor the impact of COVID-19 on these sectors and are reviewing the provision of targeted support so that core capabilities can be preserved and that the sectors can emerge stronger through the eventual recovery.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to thank the Minister for his comprehensive answer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, I note his point that the recovery in the aviation- and tourism-related sectors is likely to be weak.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second clarification is on students in affected sectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There are students studying hospitality, aerospace, aviation courses.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They are likely to have graduated this year, last year and in 2022.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They are likely to face an uncertain future.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How can we better help them to pivot or do we still continue to encourage them to enter those sectors?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The third clarification would be on helping existing workers to transit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would we be expected to provide grants, noting that many of these workers in these sectors tend to be older and find transition significantly more difficult because they have very limited runway left to transit to other sectors?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would there be a need for more concerted tripartite efforts to help them through their transition process?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But I am sure in the weeks and months ahead more of the information would come out.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we are trying to do is to ensure that as we come out of this particular pandemic and crisis, we want to be able to anchor our skillsets in that particular area and capture the growth that is going to come from that sector.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ostensibly, in the foreseeable five, 10 years ahead, once we clear this pandemic and go through this difficult period, we believe that the recovery will be quite strong.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Given our hub status, given the credibility and also the strength of our workforce, we think it is one area we can continue to anchor on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We urge companies in the growth sectors to continue to hire.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is a very good opportunity for companies to tap on our local Singaporeans as a workforce, the unemployed ones, the ones who are available and help them to pivot into different industries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In that transition, I believe that would put a lot of our fellow citizens and the companies themselves in good shape.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With regard to the other point about students being affected, indeed, this is also one of our concerns.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also have got courses that help them to ensure that they are plugged in, that when they come on board to these companies, they are in a much better position to fit in and be able to adapt and take on whatever opportunities that may come their way.
